messages:
maria: Ran a focused microbench on L40S today — testing fused-paged-attn with interleaved batch streams. seq sweep: [128,512,2048,8192], batch sweep: [1,2,4]. Observed a surprising throughput drop (~25%) at seq=8192, batch=2 compared to paged-only baseline. KV cache hitrate looked normal. nvlink/util spikes during tail generation. wondering if memory fragmentation or our allocator is tripping fused-paged kernel fallback. cc @kai @omar

kai: can you paste the exact command and the kernel selection debug output? also which compiler/driver?

maria: run command:
```
./bench_attn --model=gpt2-xl --device=l40s --kernel=fused-paged --seqs=128,512,2048,8192 --batches=1,2,4 --interleave=2 --profile-kernel-selection --out=run/211234
```
driver: CUDA 12.3, cuDNN not used, custom asm kernels built with nvcc 12.3

omar: pinged infra-bot for the node logs and GPU health. did you repro on multiple nodes?

maria: repro on 2 different L40S VMs, same host kernel. Single-GPU runs only. I attached the kernel selection snippet (trimmed):
```
[2112345678] seq=8192 batch=2 -> attempted: fused_paged_tile_v2 -> fallback: paged_flash_blocked -> selected: paged_flash_blocked (latency +30ms)
[2112345678] reason: alloc_fail? fragmentation? kv_cache_reserve=8MB, tried_alloc=12MB
```

kai: those alloc numbers look like our transient KV buffer reservation failing and triggering a path that inflates copies. can you run with `--alloc-trace` and `--force-kernel=fused_paged_tile_v2` to see if it actually OOMs or just path-selects?

maria: ran `--alloc-trace` quickly, snippet:
```
alloc: reserve_kv 8192 -> ok
alloc: temp_scratch 12288 -> fail -> retry_coalesce -> success
policy: kernel_fallback due to scratch_coalesce_latency > threshold
```
so not a hard OOM, but coalesce retries add latency and we fall back.

sasha: hmm that suggests fragmentation + coalescing overhead becomes dominant for mid batch/long seq combos. interleaving may amplify scatter in allocations. did you try turning off interleave?

maria: good call — with `--interleave=1` (no interleaving) the regression disappears (throughput matches paged-only baseline). so interleaving is a multiplier.

li: possible mitigations: 1) pre-warm a big scratch pool per worker to avoid coalesce retries, 2) modify allocator to prefer large contiguous carveouts for fused paths, 3) change interleave scheduling to avoid simultaneous large scratch requests. which is easiest to try?

kai: fastest to test is pre-warm pool and re-run bench. I can add a toggle to bench harness to allocate a large scratch buffer before kernel selection. @maria can you pick a run id?

maria: running pre-warm test now with `--prewarm-scratch=64MB` on the same nodes. will post numbers in ~10m. thanks. :hourglass: 

infra-bot: node-gpu-12 logs collected and attached to /artifacts/211234/node-gpu-12.log (sha256: a3f1...). NVLINK error rate 0.0, ECC no-corrected-errors.

omar: if prewarm helps we should add a lightweight prewarm on the runtime side for fused-paged kernels behind a feature flag. otherwise need allocator rewrite which is bigger.

maria: preliminary prewarm numbers: seq=8192 batch=2 interleave=2 -> throughput back to baseline, kernel selector picks fused_paged_tile_v2 consistently. latency tail reduced. saving full CSV to run/211234/prewarm.csv

kai: awesome. please open a small spike PR: 1) bench toggle, 2) runtime feature-flag prewarm option, 3) doc note. mark as experimental. put perf CSV + the alloc traces in the PR.

maria: will do. thanks all. filing follow-up bug with label perf/regression and linking run artifacts. :white_check_mark:
